result.title: TOGO: Take One Image Editor, Get One Video Editor for Free
result.summary: Instruction-based image editors are trained on millions of edit pairs and follow instructions far more reliably than current video editors. We show that this ability can be transferred to video editing without any training. Our key observation is that a growing number of image editors and video generators share the same latent space. Their velocity fields can therefore be combined at sampling time: the difference between the editor's velocity under the instruction and under a neutral prompt, which we call the \emph{edit velocity}, can be added to the sampler of a video model. Added naively, however, it blurs the video, alters the background and flickers. An analysis of the edit velocity explains why. It is small and reliable only at coarse scales and high noise levels, not concentrated on the edited object, and uncorrelated across frames. From these properties, we derive a simple guidance operator that amplifies the edit velocity and restricts it in noise level, space, and time. The video model then turns the incoherent per-frame signal into a temporally coherent edit. Our method, TOGO, combines Qwen-Image-Edit with the Wan2.1 video model without training or fine-tuning. On FiVE-Bench, it raises the edit success rate from 47.0\% (the same video model without the editor) to 65.6\%, above the best published method (59.2\%). At the same time, it maintains the background PSNR and obtains the best LPIPS and SSIM of all methods. Because the video editor is assembled at inference time, it can be upgraded to any newer image editor that shares the latent space with no cost.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TOGO：在共享 latent space 的图像编辑器与视频生成模型之间，把「指令下与中性提示下的 velocity 之差」作为 edit velocity 注入视频采样器，并据其仅在粗尺度、高噪声下可靠且跨帧不相关的特性，设计一个在噪声水平、空间与时间上受限的 guidance 算子，实现免训练视频编辑。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文对编辑器速度信号「何处、何噪声水平才可靠」的分析与门控注入方式，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据何时、如何注入 latent 状态以及 latent 内容可靠性判别提供可供核查的线索，但本身不研究多模态推理。
